papers.title: AdaPRA: Process Reward Agents with Adaptive Rubrics for Data Science
papers.problem: AI data science agents repeat the same checks every attempt, make coding mistakes, and waste their limited budget.
papers.fix: A supervisor agent raised an 80B model's leaderboard rank by 24.5 points on easy tasks and 14.8 on hard.
papers.practicalUseCase: If agents repeat work, a checker that remembers past attempts helps; add one to your own coding agent loops.
papers.limitation: The tests used one family of data science tasks, so other kinds of work may not improve as much.

papers.title: Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning for Search-State Awareness in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
papers.problem: AI search agents do not track what they already found, so they invent answers or stop searching too early.
papers.fix: Training agents to judge their own search progress beat the strongest baseline by 24.3 percent.
papers.practicalUseCase: If the agent knows what is missing, it searches better; prefer agents trained to track their own search progress.
papers.limitation: The gains come from benchmark tests, so real-world research tasks may behave differently.

papers.title: AlphaBet: Reinforcement Learning for LLM Event Forecasting Agents
papers.problem: AI forecasting models learn from evidence handed to them at one date, so they never practise finding evidence.
papers.fix: Training one model on many dates per event cut its Brier score from 0.731 to 0.626.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you build a forecasting agent, train it on several dates per event instead of one.
papers.limitation: The results come from one model, GLM-4.5-Air, on two forecasting benchmarks.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Almost nobody knows how sustainability sukuk issuance grew or what decides the size of each issue.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk issues, equity-based contracts, strong security, and USD or Euro denomination bring larger issue sizes.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you want bigger green sukuk, use equity-based contracts and major currencies, and keep second party opinion costs low.
papers.limitation: The data stop at 2022 and show links between factors and issue size, not cause.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan do not know whether AI and big data actually improve competitiveness and sustainable development.
papers.fix: A survey of 214 managers links AI, big data analytics, and data management to higher competitiveness and sustainability.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you run an Islamic bank, invest in AI and data systems; staff digital skill alone did not help sustainability.
papers.limitation: The survey covers one country at one point in time, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks lack clear evidence on which national factors drive growth in a system with both Islamic and conventional banks.
papers.fix: Across 218 banks, ICT adoption drove growth most, and high-tech exports helped only when combined with ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you plan a bank's growth, fund digital systems first and push for clean governance, especially for Islamic banks.
papers.limitation: The data cover 12 countries from 2010 to 2023, so other regions may differ.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Many people in Muslim-majority countries stay outside formal finance, even as Islamic finance expanded over the last decade.
papers.fix: In OIC states, income, tertiary education, institutions, internet access, population, and age dependency all shape financial inclusion.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you set inclusion policy in OIC states, spend on digital infrastructure, youth and women, and raising income.
papers.limitation: The study covers 35 countries from 2005 to 2021 and shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks form sustainability committees, but it is unclear whether those committees change real environmental work at Islamic banks.
papers.fix: Committees link to better environmental scores, but at Islamic banks only overall and resource reduction scores improve.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you judge an Islamic bank's green claims, check for real products and innovations, not just a committee.
papers.limitation: The study uses panel regressions, so it shows links between committees and scores, not cause.

papers.title: Exploring the influencing factors of academic doctoral students’ academic innovation behavior in the context of generative artificial intelligence: Self-determination theory and motivation-opportunity-ability perspectives
papers.problem: PhD students struggle to turn research motivation into new ideas, and nobody knows how generative AI changes that.
papers.fix: Both inner and outer motivation drive doctoral innovation, and strong AI literacy makes that motivation turn into innovation more efficiently.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you do research, build your AI skills and protect your motivation; good resources only partly cover low drive.
papers.limitation: The study uses one self-reported survey at one time, so it cannot prove which factor causes which.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical students face heavy testing and peer comparison, but nobody knew how often they feel like frauds.
papers.fix: Impostor feelings were frequent among medical students worldwide, though results varied a lot by sampling method and region.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you feel like a fraud in a tough program, know it is common, and seek support early.
papers.limitation: The studies differed widely, so the pooled rate is shaky and varies by sampling method and region.
